messages:
sara_sales: Hey team — POC with Acme Retail. They say free trial credits burned ~ $280 in ~24h, but their calls were light (few chat completions). Can someone look?

mike_se: Do we have example request logs or request_id? Usually that kind of surprise is either streaming counting bug or embeddings churn.

sara_sales: I have one request_id: r-0a9f3c. Also they reported a series of 429s earlier. They expected spend alerts at $100 to block further calls but it kept going.

natalie_support: Got it — can you paste the raw log snippet (no PII) and the timeframe? I'll pull the usage bucket.

sara_sales: timeframe: 2026-03-18 03:10–03:40 UTC. Log snippet from their side: ```[2026-03-18T03:12:02Z] request_id=r-0a9f3c status=200 tokens_out=1248 tokens_in=34 total_tokens=1282```. Then a few minutes later: ```[2026-03-18T03:17:40Z] request_id=r-0a9f3c status=429 error="Rate limit exceeded" backoff=1.2s```

paul_engineer: Thanks. Can you also share whether they used streaming? We recently had an edge case where streaming finalization double-counted tokens in the free-credits bucket.

sara_sales: They enabled streaming=true for chat.

oliver_billing: FYI free credits live in a separate bucket. There was a partial fix shipped last week for streaming token accounting, but some customers that started POCs before the deploy saw overcounting.

zoe_finance: Also note: org-level spend alerts are not enabled by default for trial orgs. The $100 alert may have been a project-level webhook they thought was global.

mike_se: Short-term mitigation: disable streaming or set max_tokens lower + add concurrency cap on that API key. We can also flip their routing to a dedicated small model to reduce per-token cost.

natalie_support: I'll pull the metering traces now. If it's the streaming bug, I can run a recount for that org and issue a credit. Need permission to act on billing for acme-retail@example.com (they gave consent earlier in the thread).

sara_sales: They gave verbal consent in the call. Here's last 6 chars of key: ...9f3cAB. Approve to proceed.

eng-bot: Deploy: fix/stream-token-accounting -> prod (canary 25%) at 2026-03-18T04:02:00Z :white_check_mark:

paul_engineer: I see the metering job flagged r-0a9f3c as double-counted: streaming_final_chunk logged twice. Patch pushed to dedupe final-chunk events. I'll trigger a recount job now.

oliver_billing: Per recount result: overcount = 450 tokens * 200 requests -> billed delta ~ $150. Issued credit of $150 to their account and reset trial bucket to expected remaining. I'll follow up with itemized usage CSV.

zoe_finance: I'll confirm alerts setup with Acme and send step-by-step: https://redwood.ai/docs/billing/spend-alerts and enable org-level webhooks.

sara_sales: Amazing, thanks. Can you also add a one-liner I can send the customer explaining cause/resolution?

natalie_support: One-liner: "We found a streaming metering bug that double-counted final chunks for a subset of requests; we've fixed the bug, recounted usage, and issued a corrective credit — your remaining trial balance has been restored."

sara_sales: Perfect. Closing on our end — will send the note and the CSV. :tada:
